question_1_parallel_resolution.question: Can the 123 uncertified Packs C/D Domain E+F items be resolved in parallel with expansion?

analysis.mechanics: The 123 items are in Pack C Sections E+F and Pack D Sections E+F. Expansion (Evaluate track authoring) targets Domains A/B/C/D, which are Pack C Sections A-D and Pack D Sections A-D. These are structurally SEPARATE sections within the same pack files, enabling section-level write isolation.
analysis.risk_dl019_concurrent_write: S377 demonstrated cross-session concurrent-write data loss (DL-019: 432 items overwritten when DL-013 certification wave restored pre-cleared EW[CC] fields). The same pack-file write contention exists whenever two sessions write to the same pack file.
analysis.mitigation: 1) Session scheduling: run certification of E+F items in dedicated sessions that claim Pack C/D exclusively. 2) T0 → Tend hash verification: every session that touches Pack C or D must verify the pre-session hash against the post-previous-session hash. 3) Section-level batch isolation: never run certification batches on E+F and expansion batches on A-D in overlapping sessions. 4) File-lock protocol per AGENTS.md §13: multi-agent sessions exceeding 30 minutes must run Tmid hash checks.
analysis.feasibility: Yes — the 123 items can be certified in ~3 sessions (41 items/session at ≤28 items/batch, 2 batches/session). Expansion Evaluate authoring runs in parallel sessions on the SAME packs but DIFFERENT sections. The primary risk is hash-conflict on pack-level writes, not section-content conflict.
analysis.recommended_sequence: EXECUTE FIRST: Certify all 123 E+F items (clears the known backlog). THEN: Begin expansion authoring on Domains A-D. This eliminates write contention entirely and reduces the uncertified item count to 0 → certified pool reaches 100% (2,540/2,540).

question_2_evaluate_gap_and_expansion.question: The Evaluate gap is irreducible creative labor — does expansion make it worse?
question_2_evaluate_gap_and_expansion.answer: NO — expansion IS the mechanism to close the Evaluate gap. But expansion WITHOUT a dedicated Evaluate track makes the gap persist longer.
question_2_evaluate_gap_and_expansion.verdict: EXPANSION IS THE SOLUTION, NOT THE PROBLEM

analysis.what_expansion_precisely_means: Expansion is the program encompassing: (1) Dedicated Evaluate Track — 297-item authoring pipeline at 75/week; (2) Analyze/Apply upgrades — cognitive level enhancement of existing items; (3) Certification waves — structural remediation + 6-dimension verification for remaining uncertified items; (4) DL-031 calibration — difficulty label correction. Expansion is NOT a separate workstream that competes with Evaluate — it IS the container that includes Evaluate.
analysis.why_it_doesnt_make_the_gap_worse: The Evaluate gap (297 items) is a GIVEN — it exists regardless of whether expansion is authorized. Expansion provides the dedicated resourcing mechanism to close it. Without expansion, Evaluate authoring continues at ~10 items/week incidentally during general certification (mixed velocity), extending closure to December 2026.
analysis.what_could_make_it_worse: If expansion authorizes Analyze/Apply upgrades at 21.9 items/hr while the Evaluate track languishes at 11.3 items/hr without dedicated bandwidth protection, the BLOOM'S IMBALANCE WIDENS — Analyze grows faster than Evaluate, further from CAQS §6.2 targets. This is the critical governance condition.
analysis.safeguard: G8-G10 gates (Evaluate-specific) deployed BEFORE expansion authoring begins. Dedicated Evaluate track with separate cadence (25 items/wave, 3 waves/week) — NOT mixed into general certification waves. Domain allocation plan prioritizes Domain B (62 gap, 1 current) and Domain C (61 gap, 2 current) — the domains with the largest deficits and zero clone reuse. Per CAQS §11.3 interleaving readiness, Evaluate items must cross-reference concepts from other blueprint sections, naturally increasing the overall cognitive depth of the pool.
analysis.conclusion: Expansion does not make the Evaluate gap worse — it is the only mechanism that closes it at any pace faster than December 2026. The governance condition is that the Evaluate track must be a PROTECTED workflow with dedicated bandwidth, not a best-effort addendum to general certification.

question_3_timeline_projections.question: What is the estimated completion timeline with expansion authorized vs. without?
question_3_timeline_projections.answer: WITH: 6 weeks to all-CAQS-targets-met. WITHOUT: 30+ weeks.

Execute Evaluate Wave 0 — audit all 84 existing Evaluate items, correct miscategorizations
Deploy G8-G10 Evaluate-specific governance guard rules

Deploy Rule 10 (Evaluate Scenario Sufficiency BLOCK) to governance guard

DL-031 Calibration batch 2: 18 items (per-item cognitive review)
DL-031 Rewrite Required batch 3: 4 items (stem/distractor enhancement)

without_expansion.scenario: No dedicated Evaluate track — general certification waves handle Evaluate incidentally at mixed 30 items/week total velocity, of which ~10/week are Evaluate

phase_plan.weeks_1_3: Certify 123 Pack C/D Domain E+F items. Certified pool reaches 100%.
phase_plan.weeks_4_33: Evaluate authoring at 10 items/week incidental velocity. 297 items ÷ 10/week = 30 weeks from week 4 start = week 33 end.
phase_plan.concurrent_in_background: DL-031 calibration (22 items, ~1 week), DL-032 case difficulty (optional), Analyze/Apply upgrades (incidental)

risk_factors: 10 items/week is ~1 item per authoring hour — substantially below S849 Quality-First measured velocity (11.3/hr). The velocity drop reflects bandwidth competition with general certification, not authoring speed.

By week 20+, domain coverage becomes uneven — early domains (B, C) get items, later domains (F, D) are starved. Requires explicit domain allocation, which without a dedicated track is harder to enforce.
Template regression risk is HIGHER without dedicated track governance — incidental authoring has no G8-G10 gates, no sampling audits, no dedicated reviewer. Produces more DL-012 clone waste.
Bloom's imbalance WORSENS — general certification adds more Apply items without corresponding Evaluate upgrades. Evaluate goes from 3.3% → 5% over 10 weeks, not 15%.

comparative_summary.key_difference: The dedicated Evaluate track at 75 items/week is the single variable that determines whether completion is September 2026 or February 2027. Everything else (123 certification, 22 calibration, 28 clone seed upgrades) completes in weeks 1-3 regardless.

question_4_throughput_collapse_risk.question: Is there a throughput collapse risk if expansion starts before the Evaluate track executes?
question_4_throughput_collapse_risk.answer: YES — but preventable with governance sequencing

identified_collapse_vectors.description: Multiple sessions writing to Packs C and D simultaneously (certification of E+F items + expansion Evaluate authoring on A-D sections + calibration batch 2 + DL-013 cleanup). S377 demonstrated that parallel-pack writes produce DL-019 concurrent-write overwrite.
identified_collapse_vectors.likelihood_without_governance: Very High — 4 workstreams target Packs C+D
identified_collapse_vectors.mitigation: SEQUENCE FIRST: Complete 123 certification on Packs C+D (locks Certified=500/500 on both packs). THEN: Unlock expansion Evaluate authoring on Packs C+D Sections A-D. Packs A, B, E can be expanded in parallel with Packs C+D certification (they are separate files). Section-level write isolation: no two sessions may write to the same section of the same pack concurrently.
identified_collapse_vectors.residual_risk: LOW — sequential processing eliminates DL-019 risk entirely on the two most-contended packs.

identified_collapse_vectors.description: Dual review (Accountant + Psychometrician) for Evaluate items doubles reviewer load. If one reviewer is unavailable or if review bandwidth is shared with general certification, the pipeline stalls at the G8-G10 gate.
identified_collapse_vectors.likelihood_without_governance: High — 75 items/week × 2 reviewers = 150 reviews/week, each at 5-10 min → 12.5-25 hrs/week of review. At a 25-item wave cadence, each wave needs 50-100 minutes of dual review.
identified_collapse_vectors.mitigation: Batch review: queue 25 items → Accountant reviews batch (2-3 hours) → Psychometrician reviews batch (2-3 hours) → weekly cycle. Pre-review guidelines to maximize first-pass acceptance rate. If first-pass rate drops below 80%, reduce cadence to 50 items/week.
identified_collapse_vectors.residual_risk: MEDIUM — review bandwidth is the most likely genuine bottleneck. The Evaluate track design is sound but the reviewer is human/AI time-constrained.

identified_collapse_vectors.description: Throughput pressure at 75 items/week incentivizes authors to revert to template-based bulk-authoring (DL-012 pattern). The original template pipeline produced 28 clone groups — the same thing happens at scale if governance is absent.
identified_collapse_vectors.likelihood_without_governance: High by week 3-4 of the dedicated track. Creative fatigue sets in after ~100 unique scenarios. Authors default to 'Company XYZ is considering...' pattern.
identified_collapse_vectors.mitigation: G8-G10 gates deployed BEFORE Wave 1. Weekly sampling audit: every 50 items, blind-sample 5 for G8-G10 manual review. If >1 of 5 fails, halt the wave and audit the full batch. Evaluate track has a SPECIFIC anti-template gate (G8 — named company, stakeholder, decision trigger required).
identified_collapse_vectors.residual_risk: MEDIUM — gates prevent defective items from certifying but don't prevent authoring velocity from dropping if authors must rework rejected items.

identified_collapse_vectors.description: Each batch (≤28 items) requires: governance guard (54 tests), backup protocol (timestamped backup), post_change_qc (manual invocation), pre_delivery_safety check, REVISION_HISTORY entry, and CURRENT_BASELINES hash recapture. For 297 Evaluate items ≈ 12 batches + 4 certification batches + 1 calibration batch = ~17 batches. At 10 min administrative overhead per batch = ~3 hours of admin.
identified_collapse_vectors.likelihood_without_governance: Medium — administrative overhead accumulates but does not collapse throughput. It's linear (O(n) per batch), not exponential.
identified_collapse_vectors.mitigation: Batch overhead is fixed per batch regardless of batch size. Run batches at the maximum size (28 items) to minimize batch count. Automate REVISION_HISTORY entry generation (part of the pipeline, not post-hoc).
identified_collapse_vectors.residual_risk: LOW — manageable at 3 hours total across a 6-week program.

identified_collapse_vectors.description: CURRENT_BASELINES.md §1 hashes are already stale (5 of 5 packs drifted since S377 capture). Continuous writes to 3+ pack files make baselines chronically out-of-date. When baselines are stale, T0 verification at session startup becomes unreliable → drift events are missed → DL-019 overwrites go undetected.
identified_collapse_vectors.likelihood_without_governance: Certain — 5 of 5 hashes already drifted as of S379 T0
identified_collapse_vectors.mitigation: Rebaseline all 5 pack hashes in CURRENT_BASELINES.md BEFORE any expansion authorization. Run rebuild_baselines.js (exists at scripts/, 154 lines) at end of every batch. Verify T0 hashes at start of every session. The drift is already present — fix it before adding more.
identified_collapse_vectors.residual_risk: MEDIUM — baselines will keep drifting. The question is whether the project maintains the discipline to recapture after every batch. S377→S379 drift (same day, few hours apart) suggests the discipline is fragile.

collapse_cascade_scenario.description: Worst-case sequence: V5 (stale baselines) → V1 (pack write contention on C+D) → DL-019 overwrite → V3 (template regression under pressure to redo lost work) → V2 (reviewer misses regression due to bottleneck) → defective items enter learner pool. Detection: 3-5 sessions later when a learner reports wrong explanations. Cost: 3 weeks of re-authoring + rollback + learner-pool audit.
collapse_cascade_scenario.prevention: The SEQUENTIAL RECOMMENDATION below prevents V1 entirely. The GOVERNANCE CONDITIONS prevent V2-V5. If implemented, cascade probability drops from MODERATE to LOW.

overall_throughput_collapse_risk.key_governor: SEQUENTIAL EXECUTION ORDER + baseline discipline + Evaluate track governance (G8-G10 + Rule 10)

final_determination.summary: Expansion is not an optional add-on — it is the ONLY mechanism to close the 297-item Evaluate gap this side of 2027. Without a dedicated Evaluate track, the gap closes at ~10 items/week (December 2026). With a dedicated track, it closes at 75 items/week (September 2026). The throughput collapse risks — write contention, reviewer bottleneck, template regression, baseline instability — are all real but all GOVERNOR-MANAGEABLE through sequential execution, gate deployment, and batch discipline.
